lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Coffee Roasters | Barista | Metro City, USA | Oct 2025 - Present
- Prepared drinks for the morning rush of about 200 orders and kept the bar stocked.
- Opened the café three days a week and handled the daily cash count.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: The Lumen internship and Library Room Booking project appear to attribute the same travel-search achievement to different entries and dates.
items.because: Both entries describe server rendering, a substantially shorter load time, and increased bookings, which makes the attribution questionable.

items.says: The drink-preparation and stocking work has no stated service outcome.
“Prepared drinks” does not show a barista skill or technique.
“cafØ” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “café.”
items.because: The spelling error is visible in a short bullet and can distract from the work.

items.says: Opening the café and counting cash are listed without stating what those duties accomplished.
The cash-count responsibility does not explain how the count was checked or reconciled.
The 35% improvement does not identify the performance metric.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it refers to load time, bundle size, or another measure.

items.says: The accessibility result comes after the implementation detail.
The regression result comes after the test-writing detail.
The LCP improvement is incorrectly attributed to lazy-loading the hero image.
items.because: Lazy-loading a hero image that is the LCP element can delay its loading.

items.says: React state does not prevent XSS, and rendering user input with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` can leave attacker-controlled markup executable.
items.because: React state does not sanitize input, and `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` bypasses React’s normal escaping.

items.says: The claim that cross-site scripting was prevented has no stated evidence.
items.because: The bullet gives no checkable test or verification of the security result.

items.says: The load-time and booking results are buried after the implementation detail.
The ownership claim gives no outcome for the websites or component library.
“Owned the department websites” describes responsibility rather than specific work.
“Other developers relied on” is wordy without adding a concrete detail about the library.
The result of the editor interviews appears after the interview detail.
The change from 4 seconds to under 1 does not specify what “search time” measures.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether it means system response time or the time users took to find a course.

items.says: The bullet does not say what change the app made for riders.
“Against 2.9s before” is awkward and makes the baseline less clear.
The offline-caching claim does not say how the caching was implemented.
Open-sourcing the app describes distribution, not the technical contribution behind it.
The project heading lists Vue, but the booking-flow bullet names React and TypeScript.
items.because: The entry gives conflicting frontend stacks without explaining whether both frameworks were used.

items.says: “Worked on the frontend of the booking flow” gives no outcome from the contribution.
“Worked on the frontend” does not identify what was built or changed.
The calendar bullet should lead the entry.
items.because: It is the stronger, more specific project contribution.

items.says: The calendar behavior does not describe what it changed for users or the project.
“Its tests” does not say what behavior the tests verified.
The booking increase does not name its metric or comparison period.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what “bookings” counts or what period “about a tenth” is compared with.

items.says: The impact is buried after the implementation detail, and the approximate results are phrased indirectly.
items.because: The outcomes are harder to notice and sound less direct than the evidence supports.

items.says: The travel-search-page bullet is a different project and breaks the Library Room Booking entry’s focus.
items.because: The other bullets describe room booking, so this bullet makes the project’s scope harder to follow.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “Storybook.”
items.because: The visible misspelling can distract a reader and raise an unnecessary accuracy concern.

items.says: Angular is listed without an experience or project entry that supports it.
items.because: A reader cannot find evidence of Angular use, which can make the skills list seem less reliable.
